issuer: the Korea Road Traffic Authority (KoROAD), at its driver's licence test sites, for the provincial police agencies
note: The Korea Road Traffic Authority's English guide (safedriving.or.kr, read 2026-10-30): the written test is open from 18 for the 1st Class (Ordinary), 2nd Class (Ordinary) and 2nd Class (Small) licences; the licence, issued once the road test is passed, costs KRW 10,000 for the standard card (KRW 15,000 for the mobile IC card). The tests, the physical check-up, the course and the learner's permit aren't held. The renewal page (2nd Class under 70) gives the same fee but not the interval, so the term is null (the Road Traffic Act's ten-year aptitude-test cycle wasn't read: law.go.kr didn't connect). Korea's resident registration card is a local office's and isn't held; the exchange page for foreign licences wasn't read, so no exchange list is held.
